THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE V.GOPALA KRISHNA RAO  M.A.C.M.A.No.220 of 2015 JUDGEMENT:

The appellant is the respondent in M.V.O.P.No.573 of 2012 on the file of the Motor Vehicles Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum- VI Additional District Judge, Kadapa, and the respondents are the petitioners in the said case.
2. Both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in claim application.
3. The petitioners filed a Claim Petition under section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act against the respondent, praying the Tribunal to award an amount of Rs.6,00,000/- towards compensation on account of death of Vooka Gangadhar Setty @ Chakrapani, who died in Motor Vehicles Accident occurred on 28.05.2011 at 01.45 p.m.
4.

entities.text: Motor Vehicles Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum- VI Additional District Judge, Kadapa
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The case of the petitioners is that on 28.05.2011 at 6.00 a.m. the deceased Gangadhar Setty @
Chakrapani being the owner of the motor cycle bearing No.AP 21 TTTR 8402 started from VGKRJ MACMA 220 of 2015 Krishnampalli village of Duvvur Mandal as pillion rider being driven by P.Lakshmi Narasimhulu to go to Narpala village of Ananthapur District to bring Kanakambaram seedlings, while returning at about 1.45 p.m. when they reached at a small bridge near bus stop of Korrapadu village on Muddanur-Kondapuram road, the rider of the vehicle lost control over the vehicle, resulting which the motor cycle dashed on the Northern side wall of the bridge, as a result the deceased sustained severe injuries, later succumbed to injuries and the petitioners claimed an amount of Rs.6,00,000/- towards compensation.
5.

The respondent filed counter denying the claim application and contended that the claimants are not entitled any compensation and the respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.

6. Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
i.

Whether the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the motor cycle bearing No.AP 21 TTTR 8402 owned by the VGKRJ MACMA 220 of 2015 deceased Gangadhar Setty himself that resulted in causing the death in an accident on 28.05.2011.
ii. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?

iii. To what relief?

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On behalf of the petitioners, PW1 and PW2 were examined and Ex.A1 to Ex.A4 were marked.
On behalf of respondent RW1 was examined and Ex.B1 was marked.

8. After considering the evidence on record, the Tribunal has given a finding that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of rider of offending vehicle and the Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.4,41,000/- to the petitioners towards compensation.
9. Aggrieved by the same, the respondent/appellant filed the present appeal.

10. Now, the point for consideration is:
Whether the Order of Tribunal needs any interference?
VGKRJ MACMA 220 of 2015 11.
POINT :-

The case of the claimants is that on 28.05.2011 at 6.00 a.m. the deceased Gangadhar Setty @ Chakrapani being the owner of the motor cycle bearing No.AP 21 TTTR 8402 started from Krishnampalli village of Duvvur Mandal as pillion rider being driven by P.Lakshmi Narasimhulu to go to Narpala village of Ananthapur District to bring Kanakambaram seedlings.

The petitioner further pleaded that while returning, at about 1.45 p.m., when they reached at a small bridge near bus stop of Korrapadu village on Muddanur- Kondapuram road, the rider of the vehicle lost control over the vehicle, resulting which the motor cycle dashed on the Northern side wall of the bridge, as a result the deceased sustained severe injuries, immediately after the accident, the deceased was shifted to Government Hospital, Tadipatri, as the condition of the deceased was precarious, he was referred to Government General Hospital, Ananthapur, but on the way to hospital, he succumbed to injuries.

12. The respondent/ Insurance Company pleaded in the counter itself that the policy issued to the owner of motor cycle covers own damage and liability only policy risk and the premium is collected VGKRJ MACMA 220 of 2015 covers own damage, third party liability and PA cover for owner- cum- driver and the respondent is not liable to pay any compensation.
13. In order to prove the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the two-wheeler, the claim petitioners got examined the eye-witness as PW2.

The evidence of PW2 clearly shows that because National Ins Co Ltd., Ananthapur vs Vooka Kumari, Kadapa 5 Others on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13210228/
2 of the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motor cycle only, the accident was occurred and the petitioners also relied on Ex.A1 certified copy of First Information Report and Ex.A4 certified copy of charge sheet.

entities.text: National Ins Co Ltd., Ananthapur vs Vooka Kumari, Kadapa 5 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The evidence of PW2 coupled with Ex.A1 and Ex.A4 clearly proves about the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the two-wheeler and due to his rashness and negligence only, the accident was occurred.

14. It was contended by the learned counsel for Insurance Company that the motor cycle was insured under the Act policy covering risk of third parties and owner-cum-driver no premium is collected to cover the risk of pillion rider.
Therefore, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation.
This court has perused Ex.B1 policy attached the schedule; the same is with regard to two-wheeler package policy.
VGKRJ MACMA 220 of 2015 15.

The learned counsel for the appellant relied on a decision in Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Limited Vs. B.M.Niranjan1, in that decision it was held:
A reading of the aforesaid terms and conditions discloses that the Insurance Company issued a policy known as "package policy" for two wheelers and collected a premium to cover the risk of not only own damage, but also third party.

entities.text: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Limited Vs. B.M.Niranjan1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The coverage also included the death of bodily injury to any person including occupants carried in the insured vehicle (provided such occupants are not carried for hire or reward).

The terms and conditions of the policy and the schedule of payment cannot but be said to cover claims of the injured pillion rider of the motor cycle.
Here in the present case Ex.B1 is a package policy and it covers risk of the deceased also.

16. The learned counsel for the claimant relied on a decision in L.Mini Vs. Gireeshkumar2, in that decision it was held:
As per the provision, personal injury coverage is not compulsory.
Roads to ply the vehicles are provided and maintained by the Government.
Under such a circumstance, there will be a welfare state liability for the Government, which will partially eclipse the maxim volunti non fit injuria and fault liability theory.
Liability of the Government can be made limited.

But the Government cannot elude from its limited liability in a case of accident occurring in a public 2007 Law Suit (KAR) 455 2017 ACJ 2372 VGKRJ MACMA 220 of 2015 road, where road tax is levied by the Government.

Government can either shoulder it by itself or can fasten upon the authorized insurance company by statutorily making the company liable over and above the liability of the insured when they indemnify i.e., at the moment they are entering into an insurance contract as required under Chapter XI of the Motor Vehicles Act
, they should be made statutorily liable for the welfare state liability.

An appropriate change in the statute that will make the Government/the insurer liable National Ins Co Ltd., Ananthapur vs Vooka Kumari, Kadapa 5 Others on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13210228/

This aspect needs due attention and we fervently hope and wish that it will gain deserving attention from the concerned.

Here in the present case, the rider is not the deceased person and the deceased was only a pillion rider, therefore, the facts and circumstances in the cited decision are different to the instant case.

17. The learned counsel for the Insurance company relied on a decision in Mohammed Yusuf Vs. The Divisional Manager, New India Assurance Company Limited3 in that decision it was held:
The Supreme Court in the case reported in 2004 SAR (civil) 882 has held as under:
"Section 147 does not require an insurance company to assume risk for death or bodily injury to owner of vehicle has no liability to a 2013(1) An.W.R. 976 (DB)
VGKRJ MACMA 220 of 2015 third party.

entities.text: Mohammed Yusuf Vs. The Divisional Manager, New India Assurance Company Limited3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Insurance Company also has no liability"

The learned counsel for Insurance Company also relied on a decision The Manager, ICICI Lombard General Insurance Vs. Mrs. Meena Tamang (Chettri)4, in that decision it was held:
In the case of The Branch Manager, United India Insurance Company Ltd. (supra),
the P.A. cover under the policy was to the extent of Rs.1.0 lakh (Rupees One lakh) as the premium payable was Rs.50/- (Rupees Fifty) only and the vehicle involved was a motor cycle.

entities.text: Manager, ICICI Lombard General Insurance Vs. Mrs. Meena Tamang (Chettri)4,
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case on hand, the P.A. cover is limited to the extent of Rs.2.00 lakhs (Rupees Two lakhs) on the basis of the payment of Rs.100/- (Rupees One hundred) only as premium.
Here in the instant case Ex.B1 policy is an Act policy, it covers the risk of the deceased also, therefore, the facts and circumstances are different to the instant case.

18. The learned counsel for Insurance Company also relied on a decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Ashalata Bhowmik and others, wherein it held thus:
We have carefully considered the submissions of the learned counsel made at the Bar and perused the materials placed on 2017 ACJ 2256 VGKRJ MACMA 220 of 2015 record.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Ashalata Bhowmik and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is an admitted position that the deceased was the owner- cum-driver of the vehicle in question.
The accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the vehicle by the deceased.
No other vehicle was involved in the accident.
The deceased himself was responsible for the accident.
The deceased being the owner of the offending vehicle was not a third party within the meaning of the Act.
The deceased was the victim of his own action of rash and negligent driving.

A Claimant,
in our view, cannot maintain a claim on the basis of his own fault or negligence and National Ins Co Ltd., Ananthapur vs Vooka Kumari, Kadapa 5 Others on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13210228/
4 argue that even when he himself may have caused the accident on account of his own rash and negligent driving, he can nevertheless make the insurance company to pay for the same.

entities.text: National Ins Co Ltd., Ananthapur vs Vooka Kumari, Kadapa 5 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the respondents being the LRs of the deceased could not have maintained the claim petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Here in the present case, I have clearly stated above that the deceased was not the rider of the two-wheeler, therefore, the facts and circumstances cited in the said decision are different to the instant case.
19. Here in the present case the age of the deceased is 32 years as per Post Mortem Report and Inquest Report.
By considering the age of petitioners 2 and 3, the learned Tribunal has considered the age of the deceased in between 36 to 40 and multiplier applicable to the age group of the deceased is 15.

The said finding is not VGKRJ MACMA 220 of 2015 disputed by the claimants and the learned Tribunal also came to conclusion that the income of the deceased was Rs.3,000/- per month which comes to Rs.36,000/- per annum and 1/4 of income has deducted towards personal expenses.

Since there are six claimants in this case, learned Tribunal after giving cogent reasons,
gave finding that the petitioners are entitled an amount of Rs.4,05,000/- (Rs.27,000/- x 15 =
Rs.4,05,000/-) towards loss of dependency.

Apart from that the learned Tribunal rightly awarded an amount of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate of the deceased, Rs.3,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.3,000/- towards transportation and the learned Tribunal also awarded an amount of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of consortium to the 1st claimant.

The learned Tribunal rightly came to conclusion that the claimants are entitled total amount of Rs.4,41,000/- against the respondent/
Corporation.
Therefore, there is no need to interfere with the said finding given by the Tribunal.
I have clearly stated above that Ex.B1 policy is a package policy and the schedule attached to Ex.B1 policy clearly goes to show that the said policy is a package policy.

Therefore, the respondent/
Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation of Rs.4,41,000/- as awarded by the Tribunal.
VGKRJ MACMA 220 of 2015

Therefore, in view of the above reasons, there is no need to interfere with the finding given by the Tribunal in its order for granting compensation of Rs.4,41,000/- to the claimants towards compensation.
In view of the above reasons, the appeal is devoid of merits.
20. In the result, the appeal is dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this appeal shall stand closed.

_ _ _ V.GOPALA KRISHNA RAO,J Dated: 20.03.2023.
